question: What is the adviser-fee rate on Fidelity CIAP assets? Read Fidelity Charitable's published audited financial statements (annual report) for CIAP assets and adviser-fee notes. Reconcile them with the Form 990 line 24 item "Other charitable investment advisor program" ($15.6m FY2025, $20.7m FY2024) and the line 11f contractors
conclusion_affected: Fidelity CIAP "with adviser" all-in rows; whether AEF's 0.46% generalises
rationale: The only other sponsor-level adviser-fee signal is a Fidelity 990 line that sits outside 11f. A CIAP asset figure would give a second observed average rate beside AEF

question: What is the asset-weighted in-fund expense per DAF dollar at the largest nationals? Weight published pool expense ratios by published pool assets (Fidelity, Vanguard, DAFgiving360, NPT pool fact sheets) and add it to Part IX operating cost for an all-in cost per DAF dollar comparable with community foundations
conclusion_affected: Cost-to-serve comparison (nationals 18-66 bps vs community 196 bps)
rationale: Strategic Advisers' 2025 ADV confirms Fidelity pool fund expenses "are not separately itemized or billed". GS DAF and BofA show the same gap. Part IX therefore omits a layer that could be 0.05-1.0 pp per dollar

question: Where does the Morgan Stanley GIFT advisory fee (cap 1.00%) and MSSB admin fee (0.07%) appear? Read Morgan Stanley's public ADV 2A wrap-program brochures for the GIFT fee-sharing terms and any public MS GIFT audited statements. Test whether these fees are netted inside the investment accounts, as the 990 suggests (visible 11f plus FA commissions are 7.8% of the 1% ceiling)
conclusion_affected: MS GIFT all-in row; how far Part IX understates donor-borne cost at broker captives
rationale: The circular publishes the fee stack but the 990 shows only 28 bps of operating cost. The size of the netted layer decides whether broker captives are cheap or expensive per dollar
